newsitem.title: GERMANY: Air France plans integrated cargo service.
newsitem.headline: Air France plans integrated cargo service.

text.p: Air France Cargo said it planned to build a global seamless network of integrated services for air cargo shippers.

But it had no plans to sell its capacity direct to shippers and would instead develop close partnerships with freight forwarders, Francois Bachelet, executive vice president and chief operating officer, told Reuters in an interview following a Frankfurt cargo reception.
A network of airline alliances would be built up to provide forwarders with daily services between Europe and the major world air cargo markets, he added.
Bachelet, who took over as Air France Cargo chief in January, said the "seamless products" would mirror those of freight integrators with guaranteed delivery times and a high level of reliability.
"The consequences of what this industry is going through leads us and other carriers to develop more and more a specific strategy. We have to answer the shippers' needs.
"They want a seamless product, foolproof, guaranteed, not always overnight but guaranteed and we know we have to go that way," he added.

"Today the only real response to this sort of need is the integrated way, Federal Express, United Parcel Service of America and the others. If you say Fedex, it is guaranteed and works, it is excellent."
Bachelet said he did not believe it was possible for an airline alone to offer integrated services "like some of our big, big competitors" were trying to do.
Instead, Air France wanted to build up close working relationships with those forwarders large enough and willing to develop global relationships, he said.
"What I want is that my system added or integrated into the forwarders' system adds value so that the forwarder can sell seamless products to big, worldwide accounts," he said.
"We will never build (our own) product for Ford or Unilever or Dell or whoever," he added. --Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom. Tel +44 171 542 7706; Fax: 5017
